title: tenant-stripe-allocator-for-latency-isolation-and-kernel-affinity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
High tail latency events are often caused by interleaving tenants with incompatible kernel and attention characteristics on the same runtime slice. Current stage splitters assign microbatches primarily by arrival time and coarse priority buckets; frequent kernel switches and heterogeneous attention density produce CPU/GPU kernel churn and KV-cache thrashing, increasing p95/p99 for latency-sensitive tenants.

Proposal (Stripe allocator):
Introduce a tenant-aware 'stripe allocator' that partitions prefill+decode work into micro-stripes (short-lived logical slices). Each stripe carries: tenant id, latency budget token, kernel-affinity score, and attention-density hint. The allocator will: 1) preferentially co-locate stripes with compatible kernel-affinity on the same GPU wave/front to reduce kernel switching overhead; 2) enforce soft latency isolation by reserving a stripe quota proportional to tenant latency budgets (per-tenant latency tokens), and 3) implement stripe coalescing under low load to preserve throughput.

Key ideas and why different from existing policies:
- Kernel-affinity scoring: compute lightweight score from model metadata (layer dims, quantization profile, attention sparsity), warm-run latency probes, and historical kernel selection telemetry. Use score to bias packing decisions.
- Latency budget tokens: tenants register a latency SLI (e.g., p95 goal). Allocator tracks tokens consumed by stripes; tokens replenish over time. Tenants with low tokens get priority slices or hedged micro-duplicates.
- Soft preemption + stripe hedging: allow higher-priority stripes to preempt low-priority stripes at micro-stripe boundaries (sub-10ms granularity) instead of full-stage eviction. Hedging duplicates single-token prefills when tokens are low.
- Attention-aware packing: use streaming attention-density estimates to avoid mixing dense-attention requests with sparse-attention kernels that cause memory-pressure spikes.

Integration points and constraints:
- Kernel selector: expose kernel-affinity hints to the kernel selection layer; prefer kernels that are compatible across co-packed stripes to amortize switch cost.
- KV cache: ensure stripe boundaries are KV-cache friendly; avoid splitting interactive prompts across stripes in ways that cause redundant cache loads.
- Metrics: add stripe-level telemetry (stripe_duration_ms, kernel_switch_count, hedged_count, token_debit).

Tradeoffs and risks:
- May slightly reduce throughput in pathological mixes due to stricter packing, but should improve tail latency for critical tenants.
- Token bookkeeping adds state; must be made lightweight and crash-resilient.
- Kernel-affinity heuristics can be noisy at first; require an experimental calibration phase.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator accepts stripe hints and exposes kernel-affinity to the kernel selector in canary cluster
Canary run shows >=15% improvement in p99 for latency-sensitive tenants under mixed workload compared to baseline (same throughput window)
Stripe-level metrics instrumented and visible in console dashboards (stripe_duration_ms, kernel_switch_count, hedged_count)
No KV-cache correctness regressions; run end-to-end KV cache integration tests and smoke tests pass
Fallback: when disabled, system behavior must match current scheduler (no semantic changes to billing or tenant isolation)
Operational playbook for disabling stripe allocator and rolling back canary exists in runbook
